question: Every individual real estate license issued under Iowa Code chapter 543B, including a broker license, operates on what renewal cycle?
choice_a: A two-year term
choice_b: A three-year term
choice_c: An annual (one-year) term
choice_d: A four-year term
explanation: Iowa real estate broker, salesperson, trade name, branch office, and firm licenses are issued for three-year terms, with the remaining portion of the year of issue counted as a full year. This multiyear licensing structure is authorized by Iowa Code section 543B.28 and implemented in administrative rule.
source_note: 481 IAC 2016.4(1) and 481 IAC 2003.3(2), Real Estate Commission rules (formerly 193E--3.4/3.5), implementing Iowa Code 543B.28

question: An Iowa real estate broker license issued under the standard three-year renewal cycle expires on what date?
choice_a: June 30 of the second year of the license term
choice_b: The anniversary of the licensee's original licensure date
choice_c: December 31 of the third year of the license term
choice_d: December 31 of the first year of the license term
explanation: All individual real estate licenses expire on December 31 of the third year of the license term, regardless of when during the initial year the license was first issued (a partial first year still counts as a full year of the term).

question: How many total hours of commission-approved continuing education must an Iowa real estate broker complete during each three-year renewal cycle to renew to active status?
choice_a: 24 hours
choice_b: 30 hours
choice_c: 45 hours
choice_d: 36 hours
explanation: To renew a license in active status, a broker or broker associate must complete a minimum of 36 hours of approved continuing education programs, courses, or activities during the three-year license term.
source_note: 481 IAC 2003.4(1) and 2016.4(2), Broker/Salesperson continuing education (formerly 193E--3.4(1))

question: Of the 36 hours of continuing education an Iowa broker must complete each three-year renewal cycle, how are the hours allocated among mandatory subject areas?
choice_a: 8 hours law update, 4 hours ethics, 24 hours electives
choice_b: 12 hours law update, 12 hours ethics, 12 hours electives
choice_c: 4 hours law update, 8 hours ethics, 24 hours electives
choice_d: 6 hours law update, 6 hours ethics, 24 hours electives
explanation: The commission's continuing education rule breaks the 36-hour requirement into three fixed components: 8 hours of Law Update, 4 hours of Ethics, and 24 hours of commission-approved elective coursework.
source_note: 481 IAC 2003.4(2) and 2016.4(2) (formerly 193E--3.4(2)), Iowa Real Estate Commission continuing education table

question: A broker completes continuing education hours in excess of the 36-hour renewal requirement in one cycle. What is the maximum number of excess elective hours the broker may carry forward to apply toward the next three-year renewal period?
choice_a: 36 hours
choice_b: 18 hours
choice_c: 24 hours
choice_d: No hours may ever be carried forward
explanation: A licensee who completes CE hours in excess of the renewal requirement may apply up to 50 percent of the required hours to the following renewal period, capped at a maximum of 18 hours carried forward from the previous cycle.
source_note: 481 IAC 2003.4(1) and 2016.4(2), effective 5/22/24 (ARC 7765C/7778C), current through IAC Supplement 6/10/26

question: Which category of continuing education hours can NEVER be carried over into the next renewal period, even if a licensee completed that coursework in excess of the minimum?
choice_a: Elective hours completed through distance/online learning
choice_b: Hours substituted from broker prelicense coursework
choice_c: Hours from the mandatory 8-hour law update course and the 4-hour ethics course
choice_d: Hours completed in the final six months of the renewal cycle
explanation: The carryover allowance applies only to hours in excess of the 36-hour total. Licensees are expressly barred from carrying over any hours toward the mandatory 8-hour law update course or the 4-hour ethics course — those must be freshly completed every renewal cycle.
source_note: 481 IAC 2003.4(1) and 2016.4(2): 'Licensees cannot carry over any hours toward the mandatory eight-hour law update course or the four-hour ethics course.'

question: A broker timely files a renewal application and pays the proper fee by December 31, but has not completed the required 36 hours of continuing education. What happens to the license?
choice_a: The license is automatically and permanently revoked
choice_b: The renewal application is denied outright with no opportunity to cure the deficiency
choice_c: The license renews to active status accompanied by a formal warning letter
choice_d: The license is renewed, but only to inactive status
explanation: A license may be renewed without completed continuing education, but only to inactive status. Before reactivating such a license, the licensee must submit evidence that all deficient CE hours have since been completed. This is not a denial — the renewal itself is otherwise granted, just to inactive rather than active status.

question: Under Iowa Code section 543B.28, a broker who fails to renew a license by its December 31 expiration date has how many days after expiration to file a renewal application before it is instead treated as an application to reinstate an expired license?
choice_a: 30 calendar days
choice_b: 10 calendar days
choice_c: 15 calendar days
choice_d: 60 calendar days
explanation: Iowa Code 543B.28 grants a 30-day grace period following expiration during which a broker may still renew (subject to a penalty), running from January 1 through midnight January 30. Applications received or postmarked after that point are treated as reinstatement applications under the commission's reinstatement rule rather than ordinary renewals.

question: A broker's renewal application, accompanied by the regular renewal fee, is received by the commission on January 15 — after the December 31 expiration but before the January 30 grace-period deadline. What additional amount must accompany that application?
choice_a: No additional amount is required
choice_b: A $25 penalty in addition to the regular renewal fee
choice_c: A $100 penalty
choice_d: An amount equal to double the regular renewal fee
explanation: An application received (or postmarked) after midnight December 31 but before midnight January 30 must be accompanied by the regular renewal fee plus a $25 penalty in order to be granted as a timely renewal within the statutory grace period.
source_note: 481 IAC 2003.5(2)(b) (formerly 193E--3.5(2)(b)), implementing the 'reasonable penalty' authorized by Iowa Code 543B.28

question: If a broker's license fully expires because the renewal was not filed by midnight January 30, within how many years of the original expiration date may the broker still apply to reinstate the license (rather than starting over entirely)?
choice_a: 1 year
choice_b: 2 years
choice_c: 3 years
choice_d: 5 years
explanation: A broker who fails to renew or file a completed renewal application by midnight January 30 following expiration may still reinstate the expired license within three years of the expiration date, by submitting a complete application with the regular renewal fee plus a reinstatement fee.
source_note: 481 IAC 2003.6, Reinstatement of an expired broker license (formerly 193E--3.6), implementing Iowa Code chapter 272C and 543B

question: In addition to the regular renewal fee, what reinstatement fee must a broker pay to reinstate an expired license under Iowa's real estate commission rules?
choice_a: A flat $500 fee regardless of how long the license has been expired
choice_b: 10 percent of the annual renewal fee for each year the license has been expired
choice_c: No reinstatement fee is required beyond the regular renewal fee
choice_d: $25 for each partial or full month following expiration
explanation: Reinstatement of an expired broker license requires the regular renewal fee plus an additional reinstatement fee of $25 for each partial or full month that has elapsed following the license's expiration date, up until the date of reinstatement.
source_note: 481 IAC 2003.6 (formerly 193E--3.6): 'an additional reinstatement fee of $25 for each partial or full month following expiration'

question: To reinstate an expired broker license, what must the applicant demonstrate regarding continuing education?
choice_a: The applicant must have fully satisfied all required continuing education, or have retaken and passed the broker licensing examination
choice_b: Continuing education is waived entirely upon reinstatement
choice_c: Only the 4-hour ethics course must be completed
choice_d: The applicant must complete double the normal 36-hour requirement
explanation: An application to reinstate an expired broker license must report that the broker has either fully satisfied all required continuing education or has retaken and passed the broker examination as a substitute. A broker seeking to retake the exam must first obtain written authorization from the commission.
source_note: 481 IAC 2003.6(1); see also 481 IAC 2016.9(2) (examination as a substitute for continuing education)

question: A former Iowa real estate broker fails to reinstate an expired license by December 31 of the third year following expiration. What is the consequence?
choice_a: The broker may still reinstate at any later time by simply paying a larger fee
choice_b: The former broker is treated as though never licensed in Iowa and must start over by qualifying and applying for a salesperson license
choice_c: The commission automatically issues a new broker license without further application
choice_d: The former broker is permanently barred from holding any Iowa real estate license
explanation: Once the three-year reinstatement window closes without action, the former broker is treated as if never licensed in Iowa at all. This means starting completely over in the licensing process — beginning again with the salesperson prelicense education and examination, not a direct return to broker status.
source_note: 481 IAC 2003.6(3), 'Starting over' (formerly 193E--3.6(3))

question: Which Iowa real estate licensees are required, as a condition of licensure, to carry errors and omissions (E&O) insurance covering activities under chapter 543B?
choice_a: All licensees, regardless of active or inactive status
choice_b: Only brokers, not salespersons or broker associates
choice_c: All active licensees, but not those holding inactive licenses
choice_d: Only licensees who personally maintain a trust account
explanation: Iowa Code 543B.47(1) requires the commission to adopt rules mandating E&O insurance for 'all real estate licensees, except those who hold inactive licenses.' This means the requirement follows active licensure status — brokers, broker associates, and salespersons are all covered, but a licensee who holds only an inactive license is exempt.
source_note: Iowa Code 543B.47(1); 481 IAC 2019.2(2) (formerly 193E--19.2), 'Individuals whose licenses are on inactive status...do not need to carry errors and omissions insurance'

question: Under the Iowa Real Estate Commission's group errors and omissions insurance policy, what are the minimum required per-claim and annual aggregate coverage limits?
choice_a: $50,000 per claim and $50,000 annual aggregate
choice_b: $250,000 per claim and $500,000 annual aggregate
choice_c: $1,000,000 per claim and $1,000,000 annual aggregate
choice_d: $100,000 per claim and $100,000 annual aggregate
explanation: The minimum criteria for the commission's group E&O policy require a per-claim limit of not less than $100,000 and an annual aggregate limit of not less than $100,000, applied per licensee, per claim, with defense costs payable in addition to damages.
source_note: 481 IAC 2019.2(4) (formerly 193E--19.2), Insurance criteria--general

question: Which of the following does NOT satisfy Iowa's mandatory errors and omissions insurance requirement for an active real estate licensee?
choice_a: Self-insurance
choice_b: The commission's negotiated group E&O policy
choice_c: An independently obtained individual policy meeting the commission's minimum criteria
choice_d: A firm umbrella policy meeting the required per-claim and aggregate limits
explanation: The commission's rules expressly state that self-insurance does not comply with the provisions of the Iowa errors and omissions insurance law. A licensee must obtain coverage either through the commission's group policy or through an independently carried individual or firm umbrella policy meeting minimum criteria.
source_note: 481 IAC 2019.3(10) (formerly 193E--19.3): 'Self-insurance does not comply with the provisions of the Iowa errors and omissions insurance law.'

question: A licensee fails to submit proof of E&O insurance coverage within 20 calendar days of a commission request made to verify compliance. What is the effect under Iowa Code section 543B.47?
choice_a: A warning letter is issued with no further consequence
choice_b: It is grounds for denial of an application for licensure or renewal, or for suspension or revocation of the license
choice_c: An automatic $500 fine is imposed with no other consequence
choice_d: No consequence arises unless and until a client actually files a claim
explanation: Iowa Code 543B.47 requires licensees to submit evidence of E&O compliance within 20 calendar days of a commission request (made on a test basis, random basis, or for cause). Failure of a license applicant or licensee to timely submit that proof is grounds for denial of an application, denial of renewal, or suspension or revocation of an existing license.
source_note: Iowa Code 543B.47(1) and (6); 481 IAC 2019.6(6), 'Compliance'

question: If a designated broker's license is revoked, what happens to the licenses of salespersons employed by or assigned to that broker?
choice_a: Nothing changes; the salespersons' licenses remain fully active
choice_b: The salespersons' licenses are automatically and permanently revoked
choice_c: The salespersons' licenses are automatically suspended pending a change of employer and the issuance of a new license
choice_d: The salespersons' licenses automatically convert into broker licenses
explanation: Revocation of a broker's license automatically suspends every license granted to a person by virtue of that person's employment by the revoked broker, pending a change of employer and issuance of a new license. This underscores why maintaining an active, compliant broker license is critical not just for the broker but for everyone the broker supervises.
source_note: Iowa Code 543B.29(2)

question: Under commission rule, a designated broker who agrees to sponsor a newly licensed salesperson during that salesperson's first year of licensure must be able to demonstrate what?
choice_a: That the salesperson has already passed the broker examination
choice_b: That the firm has hired a dedicated compliance officer
choice_c: That the salesperson has already completed all 36 hours of continuing education
choice_d: That the broker has the time available and the experience necessary to adequately supervise an inexperienced salesperson
explanation: The commission's supervision rule specifically singles out a salesperson's first year of licensure: a broker who sponsors a first-year salesperson must be able to demonstrate the time available and experience necessary to adequately supervise an inexperienced licensee, reflecting the broker's ongoing statutory supervisory obligation under Iowa Code 543B.62(3)(b).
source_note: 481 IAC 2007.11(4) (formerly 193E--7.15), Supervision needed

question: The Iowa Real Estate Commission generally mails renewal reminder notices to brokers in November before the December 31 expiration date. What is the legal effect if a particular broker never receives such a reminder?
choice_a: The failure of the commission to mail, or the broker to receive, a reminder does not excuse the broker from the requirement to timely renew
choice_b: The renewal deadline is automatically extended for that broker
choice_c: The broker is excused from the requirement to timely renew
choice_d: The broker's license automatically converts to inactive status without further action needed
explanation: The rule on renewing a broker license makes clear that while the commission generally sends reminders in the November preceding expiration, the failure to mail — or the broker's failure to receive — such a reminder does not excuse the broker from the independent, ongoing obligation to renew the license before it expires on December 31.
source_note: 481 IAC 2003.5(1) (formerly 193E--3.5(1)), Renewing a broker license
